why: The authors' repository is cloned and complete: the icspylab package (ics.py, scatter.py, distributions.py with generate_randu), the exact example script for the target result (examples/randu.py), and only ordinary pip dependencies (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy, numba, seaborn, matplotlib). No weights or external data files are needed because the RANDU dataset is generated on the fly inside the package, and the match target is a single unsupervised fit with explicit hyperparameters. Only small environment work is required (pip install, and optionally skipping the R/rpy2 comparison tests, which are irrelevant to C1).
blockers_seen: environment.yml is UTF-16 encoded and pins python=3.11 plus rpy2/r-ics; it should be ignored in favour of requirements.txt / pip install -e .
tests/comparisons/test_python_vs_r.py requires an R installation with the ICS package via rpy2; not needed for C1 and can be deselected
numba JIT (used by tcov/tcovAxis) needs a version supporting Python 3.12 (numba >= 0.59); first-call compilation adds a few seconds
no GPU on this machine; irrelevant since the target run is a 3-dimensional problem

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: About 3-6 minutes of command time: ~2-3 min pip install of the scientific stack (a pip install of icspylab or pip install -e . from the clone), then examples/randu.py runs in well under a minute including Numba JIT warm-up for tcovAxis. Plotting the ICS vs PCA panels adds a few seconds.

compute.basis: One 3-variable RANDU sample of a few thousand points, one ICS fit (a Tyler/tcovAxis iteration plus one eigendecomposition) and one PCA fit, so the whole cost is pip installing numpy/scipy/scikit-learn/numba/seaborn/matplotlib plus a sub-minute script; the estimate is dominated by installation, not computation.
